newsitem.title: USA: Illinois education groups call for funding reform.
newsitem.headline: Illinois education groups call for funding reform.

text.p: A coalition of education groups in Illinois called for a new school funding system on Thursday that would hike the state's income tax while lowering local property taxes.
The Fair School Funding Initiative Coalition proposed a one percent increase in the personal income tax and a 1.6 percent hike in the business income tax to raise $2.2 billion a year.
Under the plan, $1.1 billion of local property taxes would be eliminated as the state's share of school funding would grow to 50 percent from the current level of 32 percent.

"Replacing the property tax with the income tax as the primary funding source for schools will bring fairness to the school funding quation," said Ed Geppert, secretary-treasurer of Illinois Federation of Teachers, in a news release.

The group said, however, that the funding proposal is not a so-called Robin Hood plan because it would guarentee that no district would be hurt by the funding change. However, the plan would allocate more state dollars to poorer districts.

This latest school funding proposal came a day after Illinois House Elementary and Secondary Education Committee Chairman State Rep. David Phelps, D-Eldorado, announced a Feb. 19 meeting of the entire chamber to discuss school funding reform.
In his state of the state address last month, Gov. Jim Edgar called on lawmakers to pass a plan to increase state funding of schools, while reducing local school property taxes.
Last year, the Republican governor proposed a ballot question on the matter that was largely ignored by lawmakers.
